label: The de Rham Theorem
notes: This chapter closes the loop opened in Chapter 17. We knew de Rham cohomology behaved like a topological invariant; now we name the topological object it equals. Across printed pages 467 to 489 the strategy is integration of forms over chains, with Stokes supplying the bridge from analysis to topology.

label: Singular Simplices and Chains
notes: Start concretely. A singular p-simplex is just a continuous map from the standard simplex into the space, and a chain is a finite formal sum of these with integer or real coefficients. Everything that follows is bookkeeping on these maps, so make sure students see the standard simplex clearly.

label: The Boundary Operator
notes: The boundary is the alternating sum of restrictions to faces. Stress that the alternating signs are not decoration; they are exactly what makes boundary of a boundary vanish. Show the triangle whose three oriented edges cancel at every vertex, and tie it to the matrix identity in the notebook.

label: Singular Homology and Cohomology
notes: Cycles are chains with zero boundary; boundaries are images of the boundary map; homology is their quotient. Real singular cohomology is the dual, the real functionals on chains that vanish on boundaries. Emphasize that we use real coefficients here precisely so integration of forms can land in the picture.

label: Smooth Singular Homology
notes: Forms are pulled back only by smooth maps, so we restrict to smooth simplices. The key fact is that this restriction changes nothing: the inclusion of smooth chains induces an isomorphism on homology. The proof smooths a simplex while fixing its faces and adds a chain homotopy. Use the kink-to-curve cartoon.

label: Integrating Forms over Chains
notes: Define integration of a p-form over a smooth p-chain by pulling back and integrating over the standard simplex, then extending linearly. This is the raw operation behind everything. Make sure students see that a closed form fed to a cycle returns a single real number, the period.

label: Stokes Makes It Well Defined
notes: Stokes for chains says the integral of d-eta over a chain equals the integral of eta over its boundary. Two consequences: exact forms integrate to zero over cycles, and closed forms integrate to zero over boundaries. Those two vanishings are exactly what is needed for the map on cohomology to be well defined.

label: Stokes Check on the Triangle
notes: Ground the abstraction with the notebook's exact computation. Take eta equal to x dy on the standard triangle. Its exterior derivative is the area form, so the integral over the triangle is one half. Only the slanted boundary edge contributes, and that line integral also gives one half. Stokes confirmed.

label: The de Rham Homomorphism
notes: Assemble the pieces. The de Rham map sends a de Rham class to the singular cohomology class that integrates it over smooth cycles. Stokes guarantees this descends to cohomology on both sides. State it cleanly as a natural homomorphism from de Rham to real singular cohomology in each degree.

label: Periods and the Pairing
notes: Concretely the map is a pairing: a cohomology class and a homology class produce a number, the period. On the circle the normalized angular form returns the winding number of a cycle. Walk through positive, reversed, constant, and double loops so students feel the pairing is linear and honest.

label: The de Rham Theorem
notes: State the theorem. The de Rham homomorphism is an isomorphism, so de Rham cohomology computes real singular cohomology of any smooth manifold. This is the payoff: an analytic invariant built from forms and the exterior derivative equals a purely topological one built from cycles and boundaries.

label: Proof: Mayer-Vietoris and the Five Lemma
notes: Sketch the architecture. Integration commutes with pullbacks and with Mayer-Vietoris connecting maps, so the de Rham and singular long exact sequences sit in one commutative ladder. The five lemma then forces the middle map to be an isomorphism whenever its neighbors are. Naturality is the engine.

label: Proof: Local to Global
notes: Finish with the induction. Convex sets are de Rham because both cohomologies are trivial above degree zero. Mayer-Vietoris plus the five lemma upgrades finite de Rham covers, and a countable locally finite arrangement reaches any manifold. Recap that Stokes, smoothing, and naturality are the three load-bearing ideas.
